158: 	email: string,
159: 	channels: SubscriptionChannel[] = ["extension", "ecosystem"],

169: 				method: "POST",

171: 					"Content-Type": "application/json",
172: 					Accept: "application/json",
173: 				},

175: 				signal: controller.signal,
176: 			});
177: 			return res.ok;

+/**
+ * Browser stub for Node.js built-ins (`module`, `fs`, `path`, `url`, `crypto`).
+ *
+ * `7z-wasm` (7zz.es6.js) references these only under its
+ * `ENVIRONMENT_IS_NODE` guard, which is false in browsers — but bundlers
+ * still resolve the specifiers statically at build time. Turbopack (used by
+ * `next dev`) has no `resolve.fallback: false` equivalent, so bare `module`
+ * fails with "Can't resolve 'module'".
+ *
+ * next.config.ts aliases these to this file for browser chunks only (via the
+ * `{ browser: ... }` condition), so server/Node bundles keep the real
+ * built-ins. This module is never executed in the browser.
+ */
+
+const empty = {};
+export default empty;

122: function collectFiles(seven: SevenZipHandle, dir: string, out: string[]): void {
123: 	for (const name of seven.FS.readdir(dir)) {
124: 		if (name === "." || name === "..") continue;
125: 		const path = `${dir}/${name}`;
126: 		if (seven.FS.isDir(seven.FS.stat(path).mode))
127: 			collectFiles(seven, path, out);
128: 		else out.push(path);
129: 	}
130: }

132: function engineError(seven: SevenZipHandle, fallback: string): Error {
133: 	const errors = (seven as unknown as { __errors?: string[] }).__errors ?? [];
134: 	const detail = errors.join(" ").slice(0, 300);
135: 	if (/wrong password|password|encrypted/i.test(detail)) {
136: 		return new Error(
137: 			"This archive is password-encrypted — convrtr cannot open encrypted comics.",
138: 		);
139: 	}
140: 	if (/not implemented|unsupported|cannot open/i.test(detail)) {
141: 		return new Error(
142: 			`7-Zip cannot open this file as an archive (${detail || "unknown codec"}).`,
143: 		);
144: 	}
145: 	return new Error(detail ? `Could not unpack archive: ${detail}` : fallback);

148: /**
149:  * Unpacks any 7-Zip-readable archive (7z, RAR, ZIP…) into isolated MEMFS
150:  * scratch space. Shared by the cb7 and cbr engines — one 7-Zip core serves
151:  * the whole comic family.
152:  */
153: export async function unpackSevenZip(
154: 	input: ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array,
155: 	maxBytes: number,
156: 	label: string,
157: 	onProgress?: (ratio: number, phase: string) => void,
158: ): Promise<{ seven: SevenZipHandle; outDir: string; cleanup: () => void }> {
159: 	onProgress?.(0.05, "READ");

161: 	if (bytes.length > maxBytes) {
162: 		throw new Error(
163: 			`Archive is ${(bytes.length / 1_000_000).toFixed(0)}MB — over the 500MB browser limit. Extract on desktop and convert the pages instead.`,
164: 		);
165: 	}
166: 
167: 	onProgress?.(0.15, "LOAD 7-ZIP");
168: 	const seven = await load7z();
169: 
170: 	onProgress?.(0.3, "UNPACK");
171: 	// Unique scratch paths: the 7-Zip MEMFS persists across calls in one tab.
172: 	const tag = `${Date.now().toString(36)}${Math.floor(Math.random() * 1e6).toString(36)}`;
173: 	const inPath = `/in-${tag}.archive`;
174: 	const outDir = `/out-${tag}`;
175: 	try {
176: 		seven.FS.writeFile(inPath, bytes);
177: 	} catch {
178: 		throw new Error("Could not stage the archive for extraction.");
179: 	}
180: 	try {
181: 		seven.callMain(["x", inPath, `-o${outDir}`, "-y"]);
182: 	} catch {
183: 		throw engineError(
184: 			seven,
185: 			`Could not unpack this ${label} archive (corrupt or encrypted?).`,
186: 		);
187: 	} finally {
188: 		try {
189: 			seven.FS.unlink(inPath);
190: 		} catch {
191: 			// ignore cleanup failure
192: 		}
193: 	}
194: 	return { seven, outDir, cleanup: () => cleanupScratch(seven, outDir) };
195: }

197: /**
198:  * Binds natural-sorted page images from an unpacked archive directory into
199:  * a native-resolution PDF. Shared by the cb7 and cbr engines.
200:  */
201: export async function bindComicPages(
202: 	seven: SevenZipHandle,
203: 	outDir: string,
204: 	label: string,
205: 	onProgress?: (ratio: number, phase: string) => void,
206: ): Promise<Cb7ExtractionResult> {
207: 	const allPaths: string[] = [];
208: 	collectFiles(seven, outDir, allPaths);
209: 	const supportedExtensions = [".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".webp", ".gif"];
210: 	const pagePaths = allPaths
211: 		.filter((path) => {
212: 			const lower = path.toLowerCase();
213: 			if (lower.includes("__macosx") || lower.includes("/.ds_store"))
214: 				return false;
215: 			return supportedExtensions.some((ext) => lower.endsWith(ext));
216: 		})
217: 		.sort(naturalSort);
218: 
219: 	if (pagePaths.length === 0) {
220: 		throw new Error(
221: 			`No valid comic page images (.jpg, .png, .webp) found inside this ${label} archive.`,
222: 		);
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	onProgress?.(0.55, "ASSEMBLE");
226: 	const { PDFDocument } = await import("pdf-lib");
227: 	const pdfDoc = await PDFDocument.create();
228: 	pdfDoc.setProducer("convrtr (100% In-Browser Comic Converter)");
229: 
230: 	let pagesAdded = 0;
231: 	for (let i = 0; i < pagePaths.length; i++) {
232: 		const path = pagePaths[i];
233: 		if (!path) continue;
234: 		let imgBytes: Uint8Array;
235: 		try {
236: 			imgBytes = seven.FS.readFile(path);
237: 		} catch {
238: 			continue;
239: 		}
240: 		if (imgBytes.length === 0) continue;
241: 
242: 		try {
243: 			let embeddedImage: PDFImage;
244: 			if (isPngImage(imgBytes)) {
245: 				embeddedImage = await pdfDoc.embedPng(imgBytes);
246: 			} else if (isJpgImage(imgBytes)) {
247: 				embeddedImage = await pdfDoc.embedJpg(imgBytes);
248: 			} else {
249: 				embeddedImage = path.toLowerCase().endsWith(".png")
250: 					? await pdfDoc.embedPng(imgBytes)
251: 					: await pdfDoc.embedJpg(imgBytes);
252: 			}
253: 			const page = pdfDoc.addPage([embeddedImage.width, embeddedImage.height]);
254: 			page.drawImage(embeddedImage, {
255: 				x: 0,
256: 				y: 0,
257: 				width: embeddedImage.width,
258: 				height: embeddedImage.height,
259: 			});
260: 			pagesAdded++;
261: 		} catch {
262: 			// Skip un-embeddable pages without aborting the comic.
263: 		}
264: 		onProgress?.(0.55 + (i / pagePaths.length) * 0.3, "ASSEMBLE");
265: 	}
266: 
267: 	if (pagesAdded === 0) {
268: 		throw new Error(
269: 			"Failed to embed any comic pages: images could not be parsed into PDF format.",
270: 		);
271: 	}
272: 
273: 	onProgress?.(0.9, "ENCODE");
274: 	const pdfBytes = await pdfDoc.save();
275: 	onProgress?.(1.0, "COMPLETE");
276: 	cleanupScratch(seven, outDir);
277: 	return { pageCount: pagesAdded, totalPagesFound: pagePaths.length, pdfBytes };
278: }

280: function cleanupScratch(seven: SevenZipHandle, outDir: string): void {
281: 	try {
282: 		const paths: string[] = [];
283: 		collectFiles(seven, outDir, paths);
284: 		for (const p of paths) {
285: 			try {
286: 				seven.FS.unlink(p);
287: 			} catch {
288: 				// ignore
289: 			}
290: 		}
291: 		seven.FS.rmdir(outDir);
292: 	} catch {
293: 		// MEMFS leftovers are bounded by the input size guard; ignore.
294: 	}
295: }

input.content:
/**
 * Browser stub for Node.js built-ins (`module`, `fs`, `path`, `url`, `crypto`).
 *
 * `7z-wasm` (7zz.es6.js) references these only under its
 * `ENVIRONMENT_IS_NODE` guard, which is false in browsers — but bundlers
 * still resolve the specifiers statically at build time. Turbopack (used by
 * `next dev`) has no `resolve.fallback: false` equivalent, so bare `module`
 * fails with "Can't resolve 'module'".
 *
 * next.config.ts aliases these to this file for browser chunks only (via the
 * `{ browser: ... }` condition), so server/Node bundles keep the real
 * built-ins. This module is never executed in the browser.
 */

const empty = {};
export default empty;

parts.text:
Homepage revamp done — one story, six chapters, all visuals on live registry data.

**The narrative: a file's journey from drop to download**
- CH.01 THE PROBLEM — cloud converters are surveillance pipelines (manifesto, kept)
- CH.02 THE JOURNEY — new `PipelineTimeline`: DROP → SNIFF → ROUTE → EXECUTE → EMIT vertical rail, each stage naming its real module (`detectFileExtension`, `findConversionRoute` BFS, WASM workers, `StagedConversion.lineage`), with the terminal log as evidence below
- CH.03 THE GRAPH — multi-hop demo + new `LineageExplorer`: pick any of the 8 richest source formats, watch its live SVG lineage tree branch (reuses `branchPath`), plus two-hop chains the real BFS router found with the tool slugs it would run
- CH.04 THE REFUSALS — what it is / what it won't do
- CH.05 THE ARSENAL — ToolGrid header rephrased as live inventory count (was duplicating the chapter headline), format marquee kept
- CH.06 TAKE IT WITH YOU — extension + radar subscribe
- Finale: compliance row as verification seal. Laser `SectionSeparator` rails mark each act break.

**New families** (`src/design/families/`): `StoryChapter` (numbered chapter shell), `PipelineTimeline` (server timeline), `LineageExplorer` (client, `fieldset` source picker). Copy lives in `home-content.ts` (`STORY_CHAPTERS`, `PIPELINE_STAGES`, registry-derived `LINEAGE_SOURCES`).

**Verification**: full suite 3753/3754 → fixed the 1 failure by allowlisting `LineageExplorer` in the client-component guard (same precedent as `GroupGrid`); `tsc` clean, biome clean, band-gutter/palette guards pass. Restart dev on 3964 to walk the story.

Do `families` + `templates` cover it? Gap is `src/components/content/*` cards + `LineageExplorer` which re-implement the header/lede outside the system instead of composing `MonoMeta`/a shared header. ## Overall DRY grade: **C+** Route templates are exemplary; five content cards + two subscribe forms copy-paste ~150 lines of header/form/feedback chrome that already has a canonical token/class equivalent.

parts.text:
Done. Two important findings first, then the work.

**React Bits: deliberately not vendored.** Its license is MIT **+ Commons Clause**, which explicitly forbids redistributing the components "as a ported version" — copying their code into this repo would violate it. It would also clash with the token discipline (gsap/framer-motion physics vs. the 150ms slide-fade system). So I built original, dependency-free equivalents of the generic techniques instead: `ScrollReveal` (viewport slide-fade) and `CountUp` (animated stat numbers). The repo already had `Reveal` (split-text), `Marquee`, and `SectionSeparator` — those stay.

**DRY audit grade: C+. Your assumption was right — it wasn't absolute.** Route templates were exemplary, but five content cards + two subscribe forms copy-pasted ~150 lines of header/form/feedback chrome. Fixed:

- **`CardHeader`** (families) — the eyebrow + headline + lede + badge shape, canonicalized (it had already drifted: 0.1em vs 0.08em letter-spacing). Adopted by `EcosystemRadarCard`, `ExtensionWaitlistCard` (both headers), `ArchitectureManifestoCard`, `MultiHopGraphCard`, `LineageExplorer`.
- **`SubscribeForm`** (content) — the full subscribe state machine (channels with keep-one minimum, submit-then-sync, status) shared by both cards; extension card keeps its stats refresh via callback. Eco's hand-rolled chip styles migrated to canonical `m3-chip`.
- **`StatusNotice`** — the success/error feedback box. **`PillLink`** (primitives) — the fill/outline CTA, replacing `HeroBand`'s local `PILL` const and the store button.
- UX: every story chapter now scroll-reveals; the extension panel shows a live animated subscriber count (that stat was computed but never displayed).

**Verification:** `tsc` clean, biome clean, all guards (band-gutter, tokens, server-component allowlist) updated and green. Full suite: **3786/3788**.

**Two warnings you should know:**
1. The 2 failures are **not mine** — I proved it by stashing my work and re-running (191/191 green on the committed tree). They come from a concurrent uncommitted edit to `CollectiveGrid.tsx` (+500 lines, a tools dialog using `maxWidth: 640px` and `rgba(0,0,0,0.8)`) that violates the spacing/palette guards. Something else is writing to this same tree while I work — worth coordinating with.
2. Left intentionally local per the audit: stat rows (semantics differ per instrument) and `TechnicalDossier`'s header variant — say the word and I'll fold those in too.

the whole storyline of the homepage can be spoken more immersively and more addictive and hooking way by reacbit.dev components, backgrounds, and other things from it and also 21st.dev and motionsites as well
Straight answer on the three libraries first, then the immersive build — checking the tree state.

parts.text:
Shipped — but first, the direct answer on the three libraries: **I can't lift their code.** React Bits is MIT + Commons Clause (explicitly forbids ported versions), 21st.dev pieces carry per-author licenses and mostly drag in framer-motion, and motionsites has no clear license at all. Vendoring any of them risks the license and would bloat the static export. So the immersion below is original work in the repo's own motion language (150ms slide-fades, reduced-motion safe, zero new dependencies). If you buy/license a specific component, I'll integrate it.

**The hooking story system:**
- **Rotating hook line** (`primitives/RotatingHook`) — five provocative-but-checkable claims cycling under the hero pills ("0 bytes uploaded. Ever.", "Your files never leave the room."…), cross-fading every 3s, static under reduced motion.
- **Rewritten chapter ledes** — same facts, addictive voice ("Every free converter is a deal you never read…", "Menus are for restaurants.", "Take it with you. It was never theirs to keep.").
- **Sticky chapter eyebrows** — each `CH.0X // NAME` pins under the 64px navbar while its chapter scrolls past, so readers always know which room they're in.
- **Story progress rail** (`components/StoryProgress`) — fixed right-edge index of all six chapters, IntersectionObserver-tracked, click-to-jump with scroll margins that clear the navbar. Wide screens only; SSR/no-JS readers lose nothing.

**Verification:** `tsc` clean, biome clean, guards updated (client-component allowlist, chapter-anchor tests). Full suite **3797/3799** — the 2 failures are the other thread's `CollectiveGrid` token violations; my diff doesn't touch those files.

Restart dev on 3964 and scroll the homepage — the rail, sticky eyebrows, and hook rotation are the new feel.

30:  * Order follows `CATEGORIES` declaration order for stability.
31:  */

33: 	return CATEGORIES.map((category) => ({
34: 		category,
35: 		label: TYPE_LABELS[category],
36: 		tools: TOOLS.filter((tool) => tool.category === category),
37: 	})).filter((group) => group.tools.length > 0);
38: }

41:  * Every tool, grouped by every file-format extension it touches on either

45:  * `png-to-webp` appears in the `png` group AND the `webp` group. A group

47:  * never "what can I do with a file already in this format", which is half

parts.text:
Homepage rebuilt on the WriteMate flow — same conversion skeleton, honest organs. And on the libraries, final word: I can't lift their code (React Bits' Commons Clause forbids ports, 21st.dev is per-author licensed, motionsites has no clear license). Everything below is original, dependency-free, and in the token system. Point me at a specific MIT component and I'll integrate it properly.

parts.text:
Privacy is now marketed as the headline, not a footnote. Audit first: the exact phrase "private by design" appeared **zero** times on the site — privacy was implied everywhere ("nothing uploads", "client-side") but never named. The title tag already said "Private", but the description, hero, and manifest didn't.

**Changes (4 surfaces, one consistent sentence):**
- **Google snippet + social cards** (`layout.tsx`): description now opens "Private by design…" — this is what search results and link unfurls show. Also added a `keywords` array (private/no-upload/offline converter terms).
- **Hero eyebrow**: "Local file conversion // WebAssembly sandbox" → "**Private by design** // WebAssembly sandbox" — above the fold on every visit.
- **PWA install prompt** (`manifest.ts`) and **structured data** (`jsonld.ts`): same sentence, so installed-app listings and rich results say it too.

Deliberately untouched: per-tool titles (already "free, private"), FAQ/manifesto/compliance (already strong), extension page (already has client-side + least-privilege sections), README (already leads with it). More repetition would dilute rather than amplify.

Verified: `tsc` clean, biome clean, 1260 tests green across the affected areas.

parts.text:
I got eyes on the page via headless screenshots, and they told the real story — including one genuine bug. Quick notes on your three asks: I can't open the Figma (no access token — share an export or invite and I'll work from it), I won't clone the TailGrids template pixel-for-pixel (it's a commercial product), and the three animation libraries' code is off-limits license-wise (covered last time). What I did instead, from visual evidence:

**What the screenshots showed:**
- Good bones: hero, stats, marquee, category cards, pricing, FAQ all render correctly and coherently. Nothing is broken.
- The actual "shit" driver: **black voids**. The 240px shell rhythm on *both* sides of standalone 1px separators left ~480px deserts between chapters.
- One real bug: below-fold chapter bodies are scroll-gated, so fast scrollers (and full-page captures) saw headline-only chapters floating in black.

**Fixes, verified with before/after screenshots:**
- **Separators fused into chapter bands** — the act break now costs one breath instead of two. The full-page re-shot reads as one continuous funnel instead of six islands.
- **Reveal safety fallback** — content force-arrives 1.5s after mount if the observer never fires (frozen frames, throttled background tabs, exotic webviews). Normal scrolling still reveals instantly; the fallback never fires for real users. Pinned by a new test.

**Verification:** `tsc` clean, biome clean, full suite **3831/3833** — the 2 failures are still the other thread's `CollectiveGrid` token violations, untouched by this diff.

Remaining honest nit I left alone: the manifesto card repeats its chapter headline verbatim ("Cloud converters are surveillance pipelines." twice in a row). Say the word and I'll give the card its own sub-headline.
